title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II)
sample_dimensions_summary: Clear 9.525 mm diameter (4.7625 mm radius) PMMA rods (e.g., sample 218m in O15a/O15b) and 6.35 mm cohort rods inside 7.6 cm x 7.6 cm MSG flow duct.
shared_hardware_context: Conducted inside the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) 7.6 cm x 7.6 cm flow duct.
methods: Burned cylindrical PMMA rods under controlled concurrent and opposed forced airflows in ISS microgravity using fixed, changing, and staged fan protocols. NTRS 20150008961 reports the 24-test ISS concurrent-flow cohort and separate short drop-tower tests.
limitations: Table A.5 run matrix leaves run-level pressure unreported (nominal ISS cabin is ~101.3 kPa). Candidate tests O15a and O15b shared physical sample 218m (repeated-burn history) and experienced flow changes during the tests. Short drop-tower companion tests must not be pooled with ISS runs.

research_lead.question: How does step-down or changing ventilation airflow alter solid acrylic (PMMA) flame survival and extinction in spacecraft microgravity?
research_lead.finding: In Figure 6.4 the PMMA flame quenched after five progressively lower airflow plateaus as oxygen fell from 14.8% to 13.6%. O15a and O15b separately record extinction at potentiometer settings on the same rod, with calibrated oxygen recorded in Table A.5.
research_lead.conditions: ISS microgravity (MSG flow duct), clear 9.525 mm diameter PMMA rod (sample 218m) and 24-run cohort, 13.6%–21.0% O2, forced flow 0.5–45.0 cm/s.
research_lead.limitation: Does not test partial lunar gravity (~1/6 g) or the 34% O2 / 56.5 kPa exploration cabin atmosphere.

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment - I (Saffire-I)
sample_dimensions_summary: 0.4 m wide x 0.94 m long SIBAL (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass) fabric panel in uncrewed Cygnus vehicle.
shared_hardware_context: Flown aboard an uncrewed Cygnus resupply vehicle after ISS departure.
methods: Ignited a large 0.4 m x 0.94 m SIBAL (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass) fabric panel in a full-scale spacecraft module enclosure under 20 cm/s ventilation flow.
limitations: The reviewed result covers a SIBAL sheet in orbital microgravity. Run-specific numeric pressure is unreported in the cited presentation.

research_lead.question: How does a meter-scale solid fabric fire grow and interact with spacecraft enclosure volume in microgravity compared to small glovebox samples?
research_lead.finding: Sample 1-1 was a 40.6 x 94 cm SIBAL sheet aboard uncrewed Cygnus. It burned for 420 s at 20 cm/s concurrent airflow, spread at 1.8 mm/s on average and extinguished after scheduled airflow shutoff.
research_lead.conditions: Orbital microgravity in the Saffire flow duct, 20 cm/s concurrent airflow, 21.7% to 21.5% oxygen. Run-specific numeric pressure is unreported in the cited presentation.
research_lead.limitation: The flame went out at the scheduled airflow shutoff. The run does not establish a minimum airflow threshold.

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight (SAME-R)
sample_dimensions_summary: Small cylindrical polymer and wire-insulation pyrolysis coupons in MSG smoke aging duct.
shared_hardware_context: Conducted inside the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox using thermal pyrolysis of spacecraft materials.
methods: Heated materials including Kapton, cotton, silicone and Teflon below ignition, aged the smoke, and characterized its particles with aerosol instruments and microscopy.
limitations: Focused on non-flaming oxidative pyrolysis smoke particle size distributions rather than open-flame quenching or blowoff boundaries.

research_lead.question: How do microgravity smoke particle size distributions from overheated spacecraft polymers affect early fire detector selection?
research_lead.finding: Kapton run 62 count-mean particle diameter increased from 0.180 to 0.235 micrometers by microscopy and from 0.148 to 0.243 micrometers by the aerosol moment method, at 38.8 and 807.6 s of net aging.
research_lead.conditions: ISS microgravity, Kapton run 62 at 574.3 °C and 8.1 cm/s inlet velocity, with two net aging durations.
research_lead.limitation: The two observations are from the same run. Particle diameters do not establish alarm thresholds or response times.

title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
sample_dimensions_summary: Isolated 2–5 mm diameter liquid heptane and methanol fuel droplets in CIR/MDCA chamber.
shared_hardware_context: Conducted inside the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA).
methods: Dispensed isolated liquid fuel droplets (heptane, methanol) in quiescent and low-flow atmospheres diluted with inert suppressant gases (N2, CO2, He, Xe) to quantify minimum extinguishing concentrations and radiative quenching.
limitations: Liquid droplet proxy experiment (heptane/methanol); droplet burning rates and gas-dilution extinction concentrations cannot be directly pooled with solid PMMA rod flammability.

research_lead.question: How do inert gas diluents (CO2, N2, He) extinguish spherical microgravity flames, and when do post-extinction cool flames persist?
research_lead.finding: Free-floating methanol runs 203 and 171 at 21% initial oxygen and near 1 atm used 0% and 15% CO2. Their reported extinction diameters were 1.42 and 1.59 mm. Run 171 started with a larger droplet and its extinction diameter came from a fit across missing observations. Both ended in diffusive extinction.
research_lead.conditions: ISS CIR/MDCA, free-floating methanol droplets, near 1 atm and 21% initial oxygen.
research_lead.limitation: The two droplet runs differ in initial diameter and measurement method. They support a descriptive comparison of the reported outcomes without isolating a CO2 effect.

title: Lunar Gravity Combustion Investigation (LUCI)
sample_dimensions_summary: 4 mm diameter (2 mm radius) acrylic (PMMA) rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric burned at the same time in a shared rotating New Shepard sounding-rocket payload chamber.
shared_hardware_context: Flown aboard a rotating Blue Origin New Shepard sounding rocket simulating ~1/6 g; both the 4 mm acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric burned simultaneously inside the same chamber, so oxygen readings apply at shared-chamber scope.
methods: Simulated lunar gravity aboard rotating New Shepard with a 4 mm acrylic rod and cotton-fiberglass fabric burning together in normal-pressure air.
limitations: Both samples burned in the same chamber. Oxygen readings are chamber-level and numeric pressure is unreported in the cited presentation.

research_lead.question: How does simulated lunar partial gravity (~1/6 g) aboard a rotating sounding rocket affect solid acrylic and fabric combustion compared to orbital microgravity?
research_lead.finding: A 4 mm acrylic rod and SIBAL fabric burned together in normal-pressure air aboard a rotating New Shepard rocket at simulated lunar gravity. Flame-tip spread rates were 1.5 mm/s for acrylic and 1.1 mm/s for fabric. Oxygen readings apply at chamber level. Numeric chamber pressure is unreported in the presentation.
research_lead.conditions: Rotating New Shepard rocket at simulated lunar gravity, with a shared chamber in normal-pressure air.
research_lead.limitation: Numeric pressure is unreported in the presentation. Oxygen observations are chamber-level, and the test does not cover the proposed lunar rover atmosphere.
